rejected.title: Early life experiences
card: A child's early experiences can shape health and development well into adult life. The effects can last for decades.
Care
a warm, responsive caregiver who comforts a child and talks and plays with them supports healthy brain growth and emotional security.
Nutrition
a child needs enough healthy food for growth. Poor nutrition early on can affect growth and learning and can raise the risk of health problems later.
Stress
ongoing stress in early life, such as neglect or violence at home, can affect how the brain develops. This can affect learning, behaviour and health later.
rejected.remember: Care, nutrition and stress in the early years can shape a person's health long into adulthood.

a.q: Why do early life experiences matter so much for a person's health?
opts: Their effects can last for decades into adult life
They only matter until the child starts school
They decide a person's health with no later change
They affect physical growth but not learning or behaviour
a.why: The card says early care, nutrition and stress can shape health for decades. The option about deciding health with no later change is tempting, but the card says they shape health, not that they fix it.
a.clue: Think about how long the effects can last.

b.q: Lena was cared for by warm, responsive adults and ate well in her first years. Her cousin Jack lived with ongoing stress and neglect. Which is the best prediction?
opts: Lena is more likely to have better health and learning later
Jack will certainly have poor health as an adult
Lena and Jack will have the same health outcomes later
Lena's good nutrition will matter, but her care will not
b.why: Good care and nutrition support healthy development, so Lena is more likely to have better outcomes. The statement that Jack will certainly have poor health is tempting, but early stress can affect health, not fix it.
b.clue: Early experiences make outcomes more or less likely, not certain.

version.title: Early life experiences
card: Experiences in the first years of life can shape health and development for decades, because the brain is developing quickly then.
Care
warm, responsive care, such as comforting a baby and talking and playing with them, supports brain growth and a sense of security.
Nutrition
enough healthy food supports growth and learning. Poor nutrition early on can hold back growth and raise the risk of illness later in life.
Stress
ongoing stress, such as neglect or constant conflict at home, can affect how the brain develops, with effects on learning, behaviour and health later.
version.remember: Early care, food and stress can make good or poor health more likely well into adult life.

a.q: Kai is a toddler who is fed well but is rarely comforted, talked to or played with. Which statement about Kai is most accurate?
opts: The lack of care can still affect his development
Good food alone makes up for the lack of care
Care matters only once a child starts school
Care shapes feelings but not how the brain grows
a.why: Responsive care supports brain growth and security, so missing it can affect Kai's development even though he eats well. Good food is tempting, but it does not replace care.
a.clue: Food and care each do their own job.

b.q: Two cousins grow up apart. Ruby has warm care and good food in her first years. Theo faces ongoing neglect. Which prediction is best?
opts: Ruby is more likely to have good health later
Theo is certain to have poor health as an adult
Their early years will make no lasting difference
Ruby's food will matter later, but her care will not
b.why: Good care and nutrition make healthy development more likely, so Ruby is more likely to have good health later. Early stress raises the risk for Theo, but it does not make poor health certain.
b.clue: Early experiences change how likely an outcome is.

a.best: The lack of care can still affect his development

b.best: Ruby is more likely to have good health later
